record.paper_title: Billiard Dynamics: A Survey with the Emphasis on Open Problems
record.original_question: Does there exist an irrational polygon, meaning a polygon whose side angles are not all rational multiples of π, whose billiard dynamics is nonergodic?

evidence.quote: It is rational if the angles between its sides are of the form πm/n.
Problem 8. Give an example of an irrational, nonergodic polygon3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A polygon $P \subset \mathbb{R}^2$ is called rational if every interior angle between adjacent sides is a rational multiple of $\pi$; otherwise $P$ is called irrational. The billiard flow on $P$ is the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of $P$ where trajectories travel in straight lines inside $P$ and reflect from the boundary according to the law of equal angles (with trajectories hitting corners left undefined). This flow preserves the Liouville (Lebesgue) measure on the unit tangent bundle, and is said to be ergodic if every flow-invariant measurable set has either full or zero measure.

Problem: Exhibit an explicit example of an irrational polygon $P$ whose billiard flow is not ergodic with respect to Liouville measure, or prove that no such polygon exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether an irrational nonergodic polygon exists is a well-known open problem in the dynamics of polygonal billiards. Surveys and expositions (Masur–Tabachnikov handbook chapter, Schwartz's ICM survey, Matheus's blog post, and Misiurewicz's list of open problems) all describe the ergodicity behavior of billiards in irrational polygons as essentially unknown; it is known that a generic (in a Baire sense) polygon is ergodic (Kerckhoff–Masur–Smillie), but no irrational nonergodic example is known.

status_evidence.title: Rational billiards and flat structures (Masur–Tabachnikov)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys the ergodic theory of polygonal billiards and lists the construction of nonergodic irrational polygons among the basic open problems.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of an irrational nonergodic polygon is described as an open problem.

status_evidence.title: On the ergodicity of billiards in non-rational polygons (Matheus)
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses partial results approximating irrational polygons by rational ones (Liouville polygons) and states that ergodicity in irrational polygons remains poorly understood.
status_evidence.claim: No example of a nonergodic irrational polygon is currently known.

status_evidence.title: Polygonal billiards: some open problems (Misiurewicz)
status_evidence.snippet: Includes the construction/exhibition of an irrational nonergodic polygon among standing open problems for polygonal billiards.
status_evidence.claim: Problem appears in standard open-problem lists for polygonal billiards.
